react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converged on steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism as the dominant biological signal in this differential metabolomics dataset. RaMP-DB multi-database ORA returned Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism (KEGG:map00150 / SMPDB:SMP00068) and the related 17-Beta Hydroxysteroid Dehydrogenase III Deficiency (SMPDB:SMP00356) as the top two hits, both with FDR 2.16e-14 and a fold-enrichment of 1251, driven by five input steroids: dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), androstenedione, testosterone, estradiol, and dihydrotestosterone. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked hsa00140 (C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis) as the top pathway (p=1.0, 5 of 5 steroids present), confirming the same cluster. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis identified C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as its top hit (p=0.0018, 10 of 10 metabolites overlapping) and Androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and metabolism (MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism) as rank 2 (p=0.0025, 9 of 9), providing independent m/z-space corroboration that the ORA finding is not a threshold artefact. Thromboxane A2 (KEGG:C02198) independently enriched in Mummichog rank 3 (Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate, p=0.020), a known arachidonic acid–cascade product that does not appear in any ORA hit due to pathway annotation gaps for the single lipid input. Quinolinic acid (KEGG:C03722) appeared in Mummichog Vitamin B3 / tryptophan metabolism (p=0.054–0.066), consistent with its metabolic origin as a tryptophan degradation intermediate. The InChIKey reconciliation confirmed all eight resolved compounds carry distinct connectivity-based block-14 identifiers (no structural conflicts), validating that all enrichment hits represent true biological multiplicity rather than namespace aliases. The five steroidal driver metabolites collectively account for 5 of 5 input steroids in the ORA wins and 9–10 of 9–10 overlaps in the m/z-network wins, giving high confidence that the treatment condition perturbs the androgen/estrogen biosynthetic axis, with secondary activation of the arachidonic acid–prostaglandin cascade.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on steroid metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP-DB multi-database ORA ranked KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) as the top hit with FDR 2.16e-14, driven by five overlapping steroidal metabolites from the input list. The same five compounds appeared in SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at identical significance, and in REACT:R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) at FDR 1.10e-13. WikiPathways also returned WP:WP4523 (Classical pathway of steroidogenesis with glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid metabolism) and WP:WP496 (Steroid biosynthesis) as significant. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis independently ranked MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as the top hit with p=0.0012 and 10 of 10 overlapping metabolites, with MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as the second-ranked hit at p=0.0024. The m/z-network also captured a secondary prostaglandin signal: MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate ranked 3rd with p=0.0209 and contained Thromboxane A2 (C02198, CHEBI:15627). Mummichog confirmed C02198 maps to the thromboxane node in its network, establishing the prostaglandin pathway as a secondary contributor alongside the dominant steroid axis.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on steroid metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP-DB multi-database ORA ranked KEGG:map00150 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) as the top hit with FDR 2.16e-14, driven by five overlapping steroidal metabolites from the input list. The same five compounds appeared in SMPDB:SMP00068 (Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism) at identical significance, and in REACT:R-HSA-196071 (Metabolism of steroid hormones) at FDR 1.10e-13. WikiPathways also returned WP:WP4523 (Classical pathway of steroidogenesis with glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid metabolism) and WP:WP496 (Steroid biosynthesis) as significant. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis independently ranked MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as the top hit with p=0.0012 and 10 of 10 overlapping metabolites, with MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as the second-ranked hit at p=0.0024. The m/z-network also captured a secondary prostaglandin signal: MUMM:prostaglandin_formation_from_arachidonate ranked 3rd with p=0.0209 and contained Thromboxane A2 (C02198, CHEBI:15627). Mummichog confirmed C02198 maps to the thromboxane node in its network, establishing the prostaglandin pathway as a secondary contributor alongside the dominant steroid axis.
